subject: general
question: In India, judicial review is considered as:

options.text: The power of the judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders
the power of the judiciary to question the wisdom of the executive orders after they are passed by the Union cabinet
the power of the judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President
the power of the judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the legislatures

solution:
The correct answer is__** the power of the judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Judicial review in India is a power granted to the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive orders.
 
• This principle ensures that laws and executive actions do not violate the provisions of the Constitution of India.
 
• The concept is derived from Article 13, which states that any law inconsistent with the Constitution shall be void.
 
• Judicial review in India encompasses reviewing administrative decisions, legislative enactments, and constitutional amendments.
 
• It acts as a crucial mechanism for maintaining the supremacy of the Constitution and protecting fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**

 
 
• Judicial review originated in the United States through the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**.
 
• It ensures checks and balances among the three organs of the government: executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• In India, judicial review is limited compared to the United States but is pivotal in safeguarding constitutional democracy.
 
 
 
• **Articles Related to Judicial Review in India**
 
 
• **Article 13:** Declares that laws inconsistent with or in derogation of fundamental rights are void.
 
• **Article 32:** Provides the right to constitutional remedies, allowing citizens to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of rights.
 
• **Article 226:** Empowers High Courts to issue orders or writs for enforcement of fundamental rights and other purposes.
 
 
 
• **Types of Judicial Review**
 
 
• **Review of Legislative Actions:** Ensures that laws passed by the legislature adhere to constitutional provisions.
 
• **Review of Executive Actions:** Examines the validity of decisions made by the executive branch.
 
• **Review of Constitutional Amendments:** Determines whether amendments violate the basic structure of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine**
 
 
• This doctrine was established in the landmark **Keshavananda Bharati Case (1973)**.
 
• The judiciary can strike down constitutional amendments if they violate the essential features of the Constitution.
 
• Examples of basic structure elements include the supremacy of the Constitution, secularism, and judicial independence.
